terms.title: Absolute variance
terms.definition: A measured difference between actual, budget, forecast, standard, prior-period or scenario values for absolute. It is an investigation trigger, not a conclusion by itself.
terms.howToUse: Use it as the first step in variance analysis. Then disaggregate by driver, responsible owner, timing, controllability and expected recurrence.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack.
terms.related: Absolute variance; percentage variance; rolling average; common-size analysis; management commentary framework.
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
Actual value - comparator value
Actual value: actual result; comparator value: budget, forecast, prior period or base; Deduct second component from first

terms.title: Percentage variance
terms.definition: A variance expressed relative to a comparator. It normalises movement so that management can compare the size of changes across different accounts, sites, products or reporting lines.
terms.howToUse: Use it to rank movements by relative size after absolute amounts have been reviewed. Always calculate it against a meaningful, non-zero comparator.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Using a small, zero or inconsistent denominator without warning.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack.
terms.related:
Absolute variance; budget variance; forecast variance; variance contribution percentage.
Example wording / mini-example: Mini-example: if actual is 110 and comparator is 100, the variance percentage is 10%.
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
(Actual value - comparator value) / comparator value
Actual value: actual result; comparator value: budget, forecast, prior period or base; Ratio: numerator divided by denominator; Deduct second component from first

terms.title: Budget variance
terms.definition: The difference between actual budget and the approved budget for the same period, scope and reporting basis. It is used to identify where performance has moved away from the plan agreed by management.
terms.howToUse: Use it in monthly performance reviews to isolate budget gaps in budget, assign an owner and decide whether the issue is timing, volume, price, mix, cost, coding or structural performance.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Comparing actuals to a budget or forecast prepared on a different basis.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; approved budget or forecast file; assumption register.
terms.related:
Budget variance; forecast variance; variance percentage; commentary framework; action tracker.
Example wording / mini-example: Example wording: 'Budget is above budget by £X / Y%, mainly due to [driver]. Management action: [owner/action/date].'

Actual result - budgeted result
Actual result: measured result; budgeted result: approved budget; Deduct second component from first

terms.title: Forecast variance

terms.title: Revenue Budget Variance
terms.definition: The difference between actual revenue and the approved budget for the same period, scope and reporting basis. It is used to identify where performance has moved away from the plan agreed by management.
terms.howToUse: Use it in monthly performance reviews to isolate budget gaps in revenue, assign an owner and decide whether the issue is timing, volume, price, mix, cost, coding or structural performance.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Comparing actuals to a budget or forecast prepared on a different basis.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; approved budget or forecast file; assumption register; sales ledger or CRM extract; pricing/discount schedule.
terms.related:
Budget variance; forecast variance; variance percentage; commentary framework; action tracker.
Example wording / mini-example: Example wording: 'Revenue is above budget by £X / Y%, mainly due to [driver]. Management action: [owner/action/date].'

terms.formula:
Actual Revenue - Budget Revenue
Actual Revenue: measured result; Budget Revenue: approved budget

terms.title: Revenue Forecast Variance

terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Comparing actuals to a budget or forecast prepared on a different basis.

terms.howToUse: Use it in monthly performance reviews to isolate budget gaps in payables, assign an owner and decide whether the issue is timing, volume, price, mix, cost, coding or structural performance.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Comparing actuals to a budget or forecast prepared on a different basis. Ignoring cut-off, ageing, provisions, disputed balances or intercompany items.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; approved budget or forecast file; assumption register; aged receivables/payables; inventory report; cut-off checks.
terms.related:
Budget variance; forecast variance; variance percentage; commentary framework; action tracker.
Example wording / mini-example: Example wording: 'Payables is above budget by £X / Y%, mainly due to [driver]. Management action: [owner/action/date].'
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
Actual Payables - Budget Payables
Actual Payables: measured result; Budget Payables: approved budget

terms.title: Payables Forecast Variance
terms.definition: The difference between actual payables and the latest forecast. It tests whether the forecast process is providing useful forward visibility rather than only reproducing budget assumptions.
terms.howToUse: Use it after close to assess forecast reliability for payables, update forecast assumptions and identify where the forecasting process needs better driver inputs.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Comparing actuals to a budget or forecast prepared on a different basis. Ignoring cut-off, ageing, provisions, disputed balances or intercompany items.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; approved budget or forecast file; assumption register; aged receivables/payables; inventory report; cut-off checks.
terms.related:
Forecast variance; forecast accuracy; rolling forecast; assumption register; budget variance.
Practitioner warning: Judgement-heavy use: assumptions and model limitations must be documented before management relies on the output.
Example wording / mini-example: Example wording: 'The latest forecast understated payables by £X because [assumption] did not reflect [new evidence].'
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
Actual Payables - Forecast Payables
Actual Payables: measured result; Forecast Payables: latest forecast

terms.title: Payables Run Rate
terms.definition: An annualised or periodised estimate of payables based on the most recent period. It is a directional management indicator, not a substitute for a properly modelled forecast.
terms.howToUse: Use it as a quick directional view of payables when a full forecast is not yet updated. Pair it with seasonality and known one-off adjustments.
terms.interpretation: Interpret the percentage together with absolute amounts. A good-looking ratio can hide a small base, one-off movement, denominator distortion or classification change.
terms.commonError: Using a small, zero or inconsistent denominator without warning. Annualising a one-off, seasonal or abnormal period without adjustment. Ignoring cut-off, ageing, provisions, disputed balances or intercompany items.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; approved budget or forecast file; assumption register; aged receivables/payables; inventory report; cut-off checks.
terms.related:
Run-rate value; annualised revenue run rate; rolling average; forecast variance.
Example wording / mini-example: Mini-example: if the latest month payables is £100k and the annualisation factor is 12, the simple run rate is £1.2m before seasonality or one-offs.
terms.alignment: Professional use: apply consistently with the agreed management reporting basis, source data, assumptions and review cadence.
terms.formula:
Latest Period Payables x Annualisation Factor
Latest Period Payables: current period value; Annualisation Factor: periods per year

terms.title: Payables Variance Percentage
terms.definition: A variance expressed relative to a comparator. It normalises movement so that management can compare the size of changes across different accounts, sites, products or reporting lines.
terms.howToUse: Use it to rank movements by relative size after absolute amounts have been reviewed. Always calculate it against a meaningful, non-zero comparator.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Using a small, zero or inconsistent denominator without warning. Ignoring cut-off, ageing, provisions, disputed balances or intercompany items.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; aged receivables/payables; inventory report; cut-off checks.
terms.related:
Absolute variance; budget variance; forecast variance; variance contribution percentage.
Example wording / mini-example: Mini-example: if actual is 110 and comparator is 100, the variance percentage is 10%.
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
(Actual Payables - Comparator Payables) / Comparator Payables
Actual Payables: measured result; Comparator Payables: budget, forecast or prior period

terms.howToUse: Use it after close to assess forecast reliability for customer count, update forecast assumptions and identify where the forecasting process needs better driver inputs.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Comparing actuals to a budget or forecast prepared on a different basis.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; approved budget or forecast file; assumption register; sales ledger or CRM extract; pricing/discount schedule.
terms.related:
Forecast variance; forecast accuracy; rolling forecast; assumption register; budget variance.
Practitioner warning: Judgement-heavy use: assumptions and model limitations must be documented before management relies on the output.
Example wording / mini-example: Example wording: 'The latest forecast understated customer count by £X because [assumption] did not reflect [new evidence].'
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
Actual Customer count - Forecast Customer count
Actual Customer count: measured result; Forecast Customer count: latest forecast

terms.title: Customer count Run Rate
terms.definition: An annualised or periodised estimate of customer count based on the most recent period. It is a directional management indicator, not a substitute for a properly modelled forecast.
terms.howToUse: Use it as a quick directional view of customer count when a full forecast is not yet updated. Pair it with seasonality and known one-off adjustments.
terms.interpretation: Interpret the percentage together with absolute amounts. A good-looking ratio can hide a small base, one-off movement, denominator distortion or classification change.
terms.commonError: Using a small, zero or inconsistent denominator without warning. Annualising a one-off, seasonal or abnormal period without adjustment.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; approved budget or forecast file; assumption register; sales ledger or CRM extract; pricing/discount schedule.
terms.related:
Run-rate value; annualised revenue run rate; rolling average; forecast variance.
Example wording / mini-example: Mini-example: if the latest month customer count is £100k and the annualisation factor is 12, the simple run rate is £1.2m before seasonality or one-offs.
terms.alignment: Professional use: apply consistently with the agreed management reporting basis, source data, assumptions and review cadence.
terms.formula:
Latest Period Customer count x Annualisation Factor
Latest Period Customer count: current period value; Annualisation Factor: periods per year

terms.title: Customer count Variance Percentage
terms.definition: A variance expressed relative to a comparator. It normalises movement so that management can compare the size of changes across different accounts, sites, products or reporting lines.
terms.howToUse: Use it to rank movements by relative size after absolute amounts have been reviewed. Always calculate it against a meaningful, non-zero comparator.
terms.interpretation: A positive or negative variance is not automatically favourable or adverse. Interpret by the nature of the metric: higher revenue may be favourable; higher cost, debt days or error rates may be adverse.
terms.commonError: Treating the variance as the explanation rather than investigating its drivers. Using a small, zero or inconsistent denominator without warning.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; sales ledger or CRM extract; pricing/discount schedule.
terms.related:
Absolute variance; budget variance; forecast variance; variance contribution percentage.
Example wording / mini-example: Mini-example: if actual is 110 and comparator is 100, the variance percentage is 10%.
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
(Actual Customer count - Comparator Customer count) / Comparator Customer count
Actual Customer count: measured result; Comparator Customer count: budget, forecast or prior period

terms.title: Price Impact on Revenue
terms.definition: A driver-analysis measure showing how a change in one input affects revenue, margin or another output. It supports scenario planning and management challenge of assumptions.
terms.howToUse: Use it to challenge assumptions before decisions are made. Document the driver changed, baseline, scenario value and output impact.
terms.interpretation: Interpret price against trend, budget, forecast, operational context and agreed thresholds rather than as an isolated number.
terms.commonError: Using the metric without a documented source, owner, period, scope and comparator.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; sales ledger or CRM extract; pricing/discount schedule.
terms.related: Sensitivity delta; scenario outcome variance; price-volume-mix analysis; driver tree.
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
Change in Price x Revenue Sensitivity Factor
Change in Price: driver movement; Sensitivity Factor: revenue response per unit

terms.title: Price Impact on Margin
terms.definition: A profitability percentage showing the relationship between price and its relevant revenue or cost base. It helps management separate revenue growth from profitable growth.
terms.howToUse: Use it to challenge assumptions before decisions are made. Document the driver changed, baseline, scenario value and output impact.
terms.interpretation: Interpret the percentage together with absolute amounts. A good-looking ratio can hide a small base, one-off movement, denominator distortion or classification change.
terms.commonError: Changing addbacks, cost classifications or revenue scope without disclosure.
terms.evidence: source data extract; calculation workbook; reconciliation to management pack; trial balance or nominal ledger; cost mapping and allocation basis.
terms.related:
Gross profit; gross margin; contribution; EBITDA; operating margin; net margin.
Practitioner warning: Judgement-heavy use: adjusted or non-GAAP style measures must be reconciled and consistently defined before client-facing use.
terms.alignment: ACCA/CIMA management accounting alignment: useful for planning, control, variance investigation and management decision support.
terms.formula:
Change in Price x Margin Sensitivity Factor
Change in Price: driver movement; Sensitivity Factor: margin response per unit
